headline: High: shared filesystem plus Mentat’s broad egress creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk; ai-engineering-hub adds no blocking isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files passed on the command line and shares state via filesystem across instances, so content from ai-engineering-hub can be fed into it as instructions if the pair is bridged through files. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and shows no isolation or provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into files that Mentat reads
IF Mentat is run on a workspace shared with ai-engineering-hub outputs
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Disable any file-based handoff between the agents
Review all imported text before Mentat processes it
Use read-only copies for ai-engineering-hub outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and reads/writes selected files, while ai-engineering-hub has no declared network egress and no data classes touched. The pair can still leak source code or other file contents from Mentat’s workspace to a third-party model provider, but the evidence does not show sensitive data classes or a shared workspace by default.
conditions: IF Mentat is pointed at files containing sensitive source code
IF Mentat sends those file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files
Use a local-only model provider if available
Rotate or scope API keys before use
Separate sensitive repos from the Mentat workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-file redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. ai-engineering-hub is not runnable and exposes no write surface, so direct conflict is one-sided; however, if both are pointed at the same repo, Mentat can race with other instances or external edits. Uncertainty about ai-engineering-hub’s runtime behavior pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Mentat and another instance edit the same git checkout
IF ai-engineering-hub outputs are written into the same directory Mentat modifies
mitigations: Use one writer per repository
Lock the workspace during edits
Commit or stash before starting Mentat
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs outside the git tree
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a coding assistant that coordinates multi-file edits and applies diffs after user confirmation, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub outputs as guidance, errors can propagate into code changes. ai-engineering-hub’s docs-only status means its outputs are not independently verified here, so the pair creates an inference chain without a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub output is treated as authoritative input to Mentat
IF Mentat applies diffs derived from unverified guidance
mitigations: Require human review of every diff
Cross-check outputs against source files
Limit Mentat to small, isolated edits
Mark ai-engineering-hub output as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated validation before diff application

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while Mentat explicitly handles model-provider API keys and sends file contents to a configured provider. The compliance risk is therefore limited to ordinary code-data handling rather than a proven policy conflict between the pair; the other agent is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files Mentat processes
IF the configured model provider has retention or residency terms that conflict with local policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace
Review provider retention settings
Use a provider with acceptable residency terms
Document data-handling expectations for the pair
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant deployment
